description: Price the SBA 7(a) route for buying a business: the least buyer cash SBA allows (a 10% down payment that cannot be waived, at most half of it from a seller note on full standby), the loan it unlocks at SBA's maximum rate for its size, and whether the business clears SBA's 1.25x debt service cover. Terms from SBA SOP 50 10 8.1. Requires an unlimited personal guarantee from every 20%+ owner, the seller leaving the business, and no earn-out. Pass today's Prime rate; there is no default because it moves. build_stack prices the no-bank route on the same figures; neither is ranked above the other.

cash.description: Cash the buyer will put in, in dollars. Defaults to 0.

growth.description: Monthly growth percentage. Defaults to 0; growth claims are never priced in.

margin.description: Gross margin as a percentage. Defaults to 80.

mrr.description: Monthly recurring revenue in dollars, from collections where known.

opex.description: Monthly operating cost the buyer will carry, including replacing the owner. Defaults to 0, which is flagged as an unpriced owner.

prime.description: Prime rate as a percentage (the bank prime loan rate in the Federal Reserve's H.15 release). Required.

standby.description: Share of the price, as a percentage, the seller defers on full standby until the SBA loan is repaid. Capped at 5. Defaults to 0.

name: build_sba_stack
